title: SC-MT007-SessionApiSurface

scope.summary:
GOAL: Expose the session runtime as a governed API: an internal Rust service (AgentSessionService) composing store + capability registry + steer queue + supervisor + resume, HTTP routes under the existing axum API surface (src/backend/handshake_core/src/api/ — router assembled in api/mod.rs routes()/routes_with_runtime() at lines 34/65, route-module pattern per api/operator_chat.rs routes() at line 138), and Tauri IPC commands in the legacy shell (app/src-tauri/src/ — #[tauri::command] precedent at app/src-tauri/src/swarm.rs lines 7-8, command modules under app/src-tauri/src/commands/). Every lifecycle verb — launch/steer/interrupt/resume/status/list/children — is behind the existing consent/authority gates: cloud-CLI launches pass ConsentGate::check_or_prompt (src/backend/handshake_core/src/model_runtime/cloud/consent_gate.rs lines 64-133) and the cloud-lane escalation bundle discipline used by the operator-chat launch path; every error is typed end-to-end.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: (a) new file src/backend/handshake_core/src/agent_sessions/service.rs; (b) new file src/backend/handshake_core/src/api/agent_sessions.rs registered in api/mod.rs; (c) new file app/src-tauri/src/commands/agent_sessions.rs + registration in the shell's invoke_handler; (d) pub use in agent_sessions/mod.rs; (e) UserManual entry (same-change, HBR-MAN-001/004); (f) new test file src/backend/handshake_core/tests/agent_sessions_api_tests.rs.

SPEC CATALOG:

- pub struct AgentSessionService { store: AgentSessionStore, registry: Arc<CapabilityRegistry>, sessions: RwLock<HashMap<SessionId, LiveSessionEntry>>, consent: Arc<ConsentGate>, launcher: Arc<dyn SessionLauncher>, resume_launcher: Arc<dyn SessionResumeLauncher> } where LiveSessionEntry { supervised: SupervisedSession (MT-005), queue: SharedSteerQueue (MT-002), stdin: StdinWriterHandle-clone-of-sender (MT-004) }.
- pub trait SessionLauncher: Send + Sync { fn launch(&self, req: &LaunchSessionRequest) -> Result<InteractiveCliChild, AgentSessionError>; } — adapter seam over MT-004 spawn_interactive; this MT ships the production wiring type plus a test fake.
- Request/response DTOs (serde, all schema_id-stamped): LaunchSessionRequest { adapter_kind, model_name: String, cwd: String, worktree_id: Option<String>, swarm_id: Option<String>, role_overlay: Option<String> (reserved for MT-081+), initial_prompt: String }, LaunchSessionResponse { session_id, pid, capabilities: Vec<String> }; SteerRequest { message_id: Option<Uuid> (client-supplied for idempotent retry; minted v7 when absent), text: String }, SteerResponse { message_id, outcome: "queued"|"duplicate_suppressed", depth: usize }; InterruptRequest {} -> InterruptResponse { accepted: bool, receipt_expected: bool (from InterruptReceipt capability) }; ResumeRequest { requested_cwd: Option<String> } -> LaunchSessionResponse; SessionStatusResponse { session_id, thread_state, health, current_turn: Option<{turn_id, state, seq}>, queue_depth, capabilities, resumable, worktree_id, cwd }; SessionListResponse { sessions: Vec<SessionStatusResponse> }; SessionChildrenResponse { children: Vec<{process_record_id: Uuid, pid: Option<u32>, engine_kind: String, started_at_utc}> } — children come from ProcessOwnershipLedger rows whose parent_session_id equals this session (SpawnMeta.parent_session_id / ProcessStart::with_parent_session_id, process_ledger/mod.rs lines 83/174-176).
- pub enum AgentSessionApiError (thiserror + axum IntoResponse): NotFound(404), CapabilityMissing(409), NotResumable(409), CwdMismatch(409), QueueFull(429 — from SteerQueueError::CapacityExceeded), QueueClosed(409), ConsentDenied(403 — from ConsentGateError/pending decision), Internal(500, message redacted to a correlation id) — mapping table is part of the contract; every response body is {"error_kind":"...","detail":...,"session_id":...}.
- HTTP routes (api/agent_sessions.rs, mirroring api/operator_chat.rs state/builder + Router::new() shape): POST /agent-sessions/launch; POST /agent-sessions/:session_id/steer; POST /agent-sessions/:session_id/interrupt; POST /agent-sessions/:session_id/resume; GET /agent-sessions/:session_id/status; GET /agent-sessions (query: worktree_id, resumable, state filters); GET /agent-sessions/:session_id/children.
- Verb semantics (normative): launch = consent gate (cloud lanes) -> SessionLauncher.launch -> MT-003 probe registration -> MT-006 build_session_record_at_launch persisted -> supervision started -> first stdin frame carries initial_prompt; steer = registry-informed enqueue (MT-002) + drain trigger appropriate to DrainMode — steer NEVER writes stdin directly, only the drain path does; interrupt = registry.require(InterruptMidTurn) -> supervised.stop(StopReason::Interrupt) semantics for hard interrupt OR transport interrupt frame when the adapter supports in-band interrupt (seam flag on SessionLauncher — this MT wires the hard path; in-band arrives with adapters); resume = MT-006 ResumeCoordinator::resume then re-supervise; status/list = read model from store + live registry + queue depth (list merges live sessions and durable resumable records — list_resumable); children = ledger join.
- CONSENT/AUTHORITY (normative): a launch whose adapter_kind implies a cloud CLI lane calls ConsentGate::check_or_prompt(session_id, lane) BEFORE any spawn; Denied/pending -> ConsentDenied with the gate's typed decision embedded; the cloud escalation bundle fields (execution policy ref, trust class) flow through LaunchSessionRequest into CliInvocationContext exactly as the operator-chat launch path does — no new authority pathway is invented.
- Tauri IPC (app/src-tauri/src/commands/agent_sessions.rs): #[tauri::command] wrappers agent_session_launch/steer/interrupt/resume/status/list/children calling the backend HTTP surface (same-host reqwest pattern used by existing shell commands) with identical DTOs; register in the shell's invoke_handler list. If the legacy shell fails to build in the assigned worktree for pre-existing reasons, record a typed DEFERRED_SHELL_BUILD blocker in the MT evidence INSTEAD of faking the registration — the HTTP surface is the authoritative proof surface.

STEP-BY-STEP IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Read api/mod.rs routes()/routes_with_runtime() (L34-160), api/operator_chat.rs (state struct L62-136, routes L138-170) as the route-module template, consent_gate.rs L27-160, process_ledger/mod.rs SpawnMeta parent linkage L76-114 + record_spawn L147-204, and the MT-001..006 public surfaces.
2. Implement service.rs composing the five subsystems; every public method returns Result<_, AgentSessionError>; no direct stdin writes from steer (drain-only rule).
3. Implement api/agent_sessions.rs: AgentSessionsApiState with with_* builders (operator_chat pattern), routes() -> Router, IntoResponse for AgentSessionApiError with the pinned status mapping; register the router in api/mod.rs beside the existing route merges.
4. Implement the Tauri command module + registration (or the typed DEFERRED_SHELL_BUILD evidence path).
5. Update the UserManual in the SAME change: entry "Agent Sessions — launch, steer, interrupt, resume" covering purpose, the seven verbs with routes + Tauri command names, expected inputs/outputs, capability-denial errors and what they mean per transport (ACP: no mid-turn steer; transports without Resume), the cwd resume rule in operator terms, and recovery steps (interrupt vs stop, what resumable means). HBR-MAN-002 no-context bar; HBR-MAN-003 self-consistency (named routes/commands must exist).
6. Author tests/agent_sessions_api_tests.rs driving the axum router with fake launcher/resume-launcher and a real-SurrealDB store for persistence paths; an in-memory fake is permitted only for non-persistence route-unit seams and cannot prove durable behavior: (a) launch happy path returns session_id + capabilities and persists the durable record; (b) launch with cloud lane and a denying ConsentGate -> 403 ConsentDenied, NO spawn occurred; (c) steer -> queued + depth, duplicate message_id -> duplicate_suppressed; queue at cap -> 429 QueueFull; (d) interrupt without InterruptMidTurn capability -> 409 CapabilityMissing; with it -> accepted, session reaches Interrupted mapping; (e) resume wrong-cwd -> 409 CwdMismatch; (f) status/list shape assertions incl. resumable merge; (g) children returns the ledger-joined rows for a spawned fake child; (h) error-body shape pin {error_kind,...} for every failure test.
7. cargo build + clippy green; full api test suite green.
acceptance_criteria: AgentSessionService exposes launch/steer/interrupt/resume/status/list/children composing MT-001..006 with typed errors; steer never writes stdin directly (drain-only rule) — enforced by grep + review.

HTTP routes exist under /agent-sessions/* following the operator_chat route-module pattern and are registered in api/mod.rs; error responses use the pinned {error_kind,...} body and status mapping (404/409/429/403/500).
Cloud-lane launch is consent-gated BEFORE spawn: a denying ConsentGate yields 403 and zero spawned processes — proven by test (b).
Capability gating is uniform via CapabilityRegistry::require: interrupt/resume/steer degrade to typed 409s per transport — proven by tests (d),(e).
children joins ProcessOwnershipLedger rows by parent_session_id — proven by test (g).
Tauri commands agent_session_* registered in the shell invoke_handler OR a typed DEFERRED_SHELL_BUILD blocker recorded with the exact build failure; never silent omission.
UserManual updated in the SAME change with the no-context entry described in step 5; self-consistency check passes (HBR-MAN-003).
cargo build -p handshake_core green; clippy clean; api test suite green.
proof_targets: cargo test -p handshake_core agent_sessions_api --nocapture 2>&1 | tee /tmp/mt007_run.txt && grep -E 'test result: ok' /tmp/mt007_run.txt
expected_tests: router-driven happy paths for all 7 verbs
children ledger join; error-body shape pins
implementation_notes: The service composes; it must not re-implement: queue rules live in MT-002, capability denial in MT-003 require(), stop semantics in MT-005, cwd rules in MT-006. Any duplicated rule here is a review-rejectable defect.

Interrupt duality: hard interrupt (supervisor stop with StopReason::Interrupt) always works; in-band transport interrupt (Claude interrupt frame with interrupt_receipt_v1 acks, Codex turn/interrupt) is adapter-family work — the seam is receipt_expected driven by the InterruptReceipt capability so the GUI can show 'interrupt acknowledged' only when truthful.

List merge rule: live sessions (in-memory map) take precedence over durable records with the same session_id; durable-only rows appear with health=Exited and their resumable flag — this is what the GUI session pane binds to.
The Tauri layer is a thin relay to HTTP (one source of truth for authority/consent); do NOT re-wire service objects into the shell process.
HBR-SWARM-004 applies to steer/interrupt DTOs: message_id is the correlation id; SteerResponse echoes it; MT-008 receipts extend the same id space — no narrative-only routing.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: API-surface MT: HTTP + IPC endpoints only; the operator GUI panes that consume these routes are the GUI family's MTs, which carry the Argus obligations for the visible surface.

target_entries: Agent Sessions — launch, steer, interrupt, resume (routes /agent-sessions/*, Tauri commands agent_session_*)
Agent Sessions — capability-denial errors per transport (steer/interrupt/resume availability, ACP limitations)
Agent Sessions — resume cwd/worktree rule and recovery steps

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations: internal_diagnostics (may be typed DEFERRED if the internal-diagnostics tier is not yet shipped for agent_sessions)
palmistry (may be typed DEFERRED if palmistry wiring is not yet shipped for agent_sessions)
risk_if_missed: The session runtime stays library-only: no operator or model can launch/steer/resume a session, no consent gating exists for long-lived cloud lanes, and the GUI/orchestrator families have no endpoint to bind — WP-017 delivers no usable behavior.

risks: RISK-1: Consent bypass — a launch path that spawns a cloud CLI before ConsentGate resolves, or a resume path that skips the gate entirely, burns operator spend without authority.
RISK-2: Steer race to stdin — a 'fast path' writing steer text directly to stdin bypasses queue ordering/dup-suppression and re-creates every MT-002 failure mode.
RISK-3: Error laundering — Internal(500) leaking raw process/store errors (paths, SQL) to HTTP/IPC clients.
RISK-4: Shell drift — Tauri commands silently unregistered or diverging DTOs, so the shell shows different truth than HTTP clients.
RISK-5: Manual drift — routes ship without the same-change UserManual entry, leaving no-context models unable to operate sessions (HBR-MAN violation).
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): consent check is the FIRST statement of launch AND resume for cloud lanes; test (b) proves zero spawn on deny; validator greps call order.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): drain-only rule is normative; grep proof that service.rs steer path never references StdinWriterHandle::write_frame; queue tests re-run through the router.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): Internal variant carries only a correlation id; body-shape pin test asserts no raw error strings in 500 bodies.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): shared DTO types serialized identically on both surfaces; registration is an acceptance criterion with typed DEFERRED_SHELL_BUILD as the only alternative.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): same_change_update_required=YES + HBR-MAN-003 self-consistency test named in proof targets.

surrealdb_authority_v02_205.supersedes: Any PostgreSQL, Postgres, PgPool, sqlx-postgres, SQL-DDL, JSONB, RLS, LISTEN-NOTIFY, pgvector, DATABASE_URL, PostgreSQL test-container, or PostgreSQL proof instruction elsewhere in this pre-pivot contract.
surrealdb_authority_v02_205.implementation_rule: When this MT reads or writes durable product state it MUST use the typed SurrealDB boundary created by MT-331..MT-334 and the authenticated record-user plus ResourceBroker privacy contract from MT-333. It MUST NOT add a PostgreSQL fallback, parallel authority, direct pool escape, or runtime dependency.
surrealdb_authority_v02_205.proof_rule: PostgreSQL-era fixtures and historical receipts do not prove this MT. Fresh real-SurrealDB proof is required for every storage-affected acceptance criterion; administrative SurrealDB credentials cannot prove privacy.
surrealdb_authority_v02_205.postgresql_data_migration: NOT_REQUIRED: the current PostgreSQL database contains no valuable live information. No MT may connect to it, import from it, fall back to it, or use it as proof.

surrealdb_translation_v02_205.schema_rule: Any embedded PostgreSQL DDL/SQL snippet is a semantic field/index/invariant inventory only. Implement it as SCHEMAFULL SurrealQL through SurrealKit; do not execute or mechanically transliterate the snippet.
surrealdb_translation_v02_205.concurrency_rule: Translate advisory locks, SKIP LOCKED and row locks into SurrealDB transactions, durable lease/fencing records and conditional updates with equivalent tests.
surrealdb_translation_v02_205.notification_rule: Translate LISTEN/NOTIFY into scoped SurrealDB live queries plus bounded resynchronization.
surrealdb_translation_v02_205.privacy_rule: Translate RLS into authenticated record-user table/field PERMISSIONS intersected with ResourceBroker; administrative credentials cannot prove privacy.
surrealdb_translation_v02_205.proof_rule: All named storage proofs run against real SurrealDB. No PostgreSQL process, driver, connection, fixture, environment variable or fallback is permitted.
